transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-07-14
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CTO, Arcadia), Samir Patel (Lead ML Eng, Arcadia), Olivia Chen (Security, Arcadia)

Summary: quick PLG discovery for Redwood API; Arcadia wants fast time-to-first-token for a pilot; evaluating hosted now but may need Dedicated or Private for production; security questions re: SOC2, KMS, VPC.

[00:00:05] Lena (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Lena AE at Redwood, with Marco our solutions engineer. Quick intros?
[00:00:20] Priya (Arcadia): Hi I'm Priya, CTO at Arcadia Systems, we build a customer support assistant, currently prototyping with OpenAI but want lower unit cost and more predictable perf.
[00:00:35] Samir: Samir here, lead ML eng. We're most interested in embeddings for semantic search and a low-latency chat front-end, target QPS ~40-60 at peak.
[00:00:50] Olivia: Olivia, security — I'll be focused on compliance and data residency.
[00:01:10] Marco (Redwood): Great, quick agenda: PLG quickstart flow, free credits/time-to-first-token, then discuss hosted vs dedicated vs private and security. Open Qs anytime.
[00:01:35] Priya: Sounds good — our timeline is tight; pilot in 2 weeks ideally, production in 2-3 months.
[00:01:50] Lena: Totally reasonable. For PLG quickstart we can get you an org + API key and $2k free credits — typical time-to-first-token is under 10 minutes with our SDKs and quickstart repo.
[00:02:10] Samir: When you say under 10 minutes, that's dev-time or token latency? We care about both.
[00:02:20] Marco: dev-time — meaning code + key, run sample request and get responses. For latency, hosted API P50 for mid-sized open models is often in the 100-200ms per-token range depending on model and seq len; we can show specific numbers in the benchmark.
[00:02:40] Priya: Ok, and cost comparison vs OpenAI — any ballpark?
[00:02:50] Lena: Depends on model choice, quantization, and batching. In many cases customers see 20-50% lower unit cost using our curated open models and batching/caching suggestions. We'll include a cost estimator in the trial docs.
[00:03:10] Olivia: Security first: is Redwood SOC 2? what about SSO and audit logs?
[00:03:20] Marco: Redwood's hosted offering is SOC 2 compliant; we provide SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and optional longer retention on logs as an add-on. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and VPC options.
[00:03:40] Olivia: Great. Data residency — do you allow region pinning?
[00:03:50] Lena: Yes, hosted can be region-backed and Dedicated/Private gives you full control. We'll share the region map and residency options.
[00:04:05] Samir: For the pilot we probably want hosted to move fast, but we need a path to Dedicated later for latency SLAs. How painless is that migration?
[00:04:20] Marco: We keep the same API surface; you can pin model versions and rollout policies while switching deployment mode. We also provide migration playbooks. It's usually straightforward — mainly config and provisioning.
[00:04:40] Priya: What's the isolation on Dedicated? Are there noisy neighbors concerns?
[00:04:50] Marco: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput and isolation. We also offer burst capacity options and autoscaling policies so you don't hit sudden throttles.
[00:05:10] Lena: Quick qualification: what's your data classification — any PII or regulated data in the pilot?
[00:05:20] Samir: We'll use anonymized transcripts initially, but production will touch PII, so we need KMS encryption and auditability.
[00:05:35] Olivia: And we need to confirm log retention policies and ability to disable data retention for hosted vs pass-through to our storage.
[00:05:50] Marco: For hosted we have data retention options and the option to turn off retention for certain customers; Private gives you full control to keep things in your VPC / on-prem.
[00:06:10] Priya: Good. On features: do you support streaming, function calling and structured output? That's critical for our UI.
[00:06:20] Marco: Yes — streaming responses, function-calling and structured output supported in the API and SDKs. We'll send example payloads.
[00:06:35] Samir: What's the SDK language support? Node, Python?
[00:06:40] Lena: Node, Python, and REST. We also have a quickstart repo with examples.
[00:06:55] [00:07:05] Priya: For evaluation, Samir will run embedding recall tests and latency tests. Any recommended baseline models?
[00:07:15] Marco: For embeddings we often recommend model-x-embedding-1 (curated open model) as a cost-effective choice; for chat small/medium models to start — we can map to your latency targets.
[00:07:30] Samir: Could you share quantization options? We may want 4-bit variants for Dedicated to reduce cost.
[00:07:40] Marco: Absolutely. We provide quantization profiles and recommend kernels per hardware. For Dedicated we can run 4-bit optimizations to reduce memory and improve throughput.
[00:07:55] Olivia: On the legal side, any standard DPA / data processing terms?
[00:08:05] Lena: Yes — we'll include the DPA and SOC 2 report in the security pack.
[00:08:20] [00:08:35] Priya: Ok, success criteria for pilot: embeddings recall > 90% on our eval set, median chat latency under 200ms, and predictable unit cost that beats our current baseline. If we hit those in 2 weeks we'll expand to a Dedicated POC.
[00:08:55] Lena: Sounds clear. We'll aim to help you hit that. I'll provision the trial org and credits today.
[00:09:10] Samir: On benchmarks — any recommended test harness? we've used wrk and custom prompts; do you have a template?
[00:09:20] Marco: Yes we have a benchmark guide for QPS/latency that includes sample promps, batching configs, and KV cache suggestions. I'll share a template.
[00:09:40] Priya: A few technical Qs — do you support prefix caching or KV cache for chat?
[00:09:50] Marco: We support prefix/KV caching and automatic cache reuse for conversation patterns — this often reduces per-token compute costs and latency.
[00:10:05] Samir: Any throttling policy on free trials that will affect the benchmark?
[00:10:15] Lena: Trials have reasonable quotas but we can allocate dedicated trial capacity for benchmark sessions so you get honest numbers. We'll note that in the trial.
[00:10:30] Olivia: For SSO — we use Okta. We need SAML and SCIM for provisioning.
[00:10:40] Marco: Okta SAML and SCIM are supported; we'll include setup steps.
[00:10:55] [00:11:10] Priya: One more — if we go with hosted initially, how do you handle secrets / KMS?
[00:11:20] Marco: Hosted customers can use Redwood-managed KMS, but for Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own) and HSM in Private.
[00:11:35] Samir: Are there per-request headers for tracing and token breakdowns? We want tracing to map cost to user actions.
[00:11:45] Lena: Yes, we provide token-level cost and latency breakdowns in Redwood Console, plus tracing hooks you can send to your observability system.
[00:12:00] [00:12:20] Priya: Anything we should watch for moving from pilot to production? common gotchas?
[00:12:30] Marco: Two things — batching configuration and KV cache tuning; also model selection for quality vs latency. We usually run a short tuning phase.
[00:12:45] Samir: For model fallbacks, can you auto-route to cheaper variants if capacity is constrained?
[00:12:55] Marco: Yes, smart routing policies can fallback to compatible model variants by policy (latency, cost, or region).
[00:13:10] Priya: Great. On pricing — is there a committed contract for Dedicated? typical terms?
[00:13:20] Lena: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits; we can provide a sample pricing sheet. For pilot you'll be usage-based.
[00:13:35] Olivia: And SLA targets for Dedicated?
[00:13:40] Marco: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include SLA language in the pack.
[00:13:55] [00:14:15] Priya: Ok, for next steps can we recap?
[00:14:20] Lena: Sure — 1) I'll provision trial org + $2k credits and send quickstart steps + SDK samples (Lena) by tomorrow; 2) Marco will share benchmark guide, quantization docs, and security pack incl SOC2 and DPA (Marco) by 7/16; 3) schedule a bench session with Samir — target 7/20.
[00:14:45] Samir: I'll send our prompt set and eval metrics by 7/18.
[00:14:55] Olivia: I'll review security docs and come back with any gaps by 7/16.
[00:15:10] Lena: Great. Anything else?
[00:15:15] Priya: One small question — do you support private deployments on-prem if we need air-gapped?
[00:15:25] Marco: Yes, Private includes on-prem air-gapped options with a customer control plane and optional HSM. We'll outline the process.
[00:15:40] [00:16:05] Priya: Nice. Could you also include sample data deletion/retention APIs?
[00:16:15] Marco: Yes, we'll include retention and deletion endpoints in the security docs.
[00:16:30] Samir: On embeddings — how do you handle incremental reindexing? any differential update APIs?
[00:16:40] Marco: We provide batching and streaming ingest paths and recommend incremental reindexing patterns; we'll add examples.
[00:16:55] Lena: Ok folks, last checkpoints: I'll send the trial invite and credentials now after the call. Marco will follow up on technical docs. We'll tentatively schedule the benchmark for 7/20.
[00:17:10] [00:17:30] Priya: Thanks everyone. This was helpful and clear.
[00:17:40] Lena: Thanks — we'll follow up.

End of meeting notes.

Notes: transcript has occasional transcription errors; product names spelled variably in conversation (e.g., model-x, model y) — this mirrors real fireflies exports.
